rationale: The durable term regression is the most severe claim of this run and so far rests on one execution, so this turn spends one execution on reproducing it rather than on widening scope. The question the repeat asks is narrow and worth asking: does the same interleaving occur on a fresh schedule, and does it produce the same shape of result - the fast-path heartbeat's term adopted in memory and in the stable store, then overwritten by the election write that was held open - or does the second run come out differently, which would tell me the first was an artefact of how that particular schedule lined up. The harness is unchanged and retained, so this is schedule variation of one scenario rather than a new setup. Two things I want on the record with it, because they are the strongest objections to the claim as stated. First, the scenario is not as contrived as a single-voter run may suggest: in a real cluster the node that interleaves is one that has lagged behind its leader, so it is exactly a node that starts an election on its own while the leader, whose term is several ahead of it, is still trying to reach it - the heartbeat that carries the higher term is the leader's own, not a harness invention, and the election is the node's ordinary response to not having heard from anyone. The instrumented store does not create that ordering, it only holds the existing interval open so the interleaving can be observed rather than missed. Second, the durability half is what makes the outcome matter: the fast path persists the higher term before the election's write persists the lower one, so the stable store ends up recording a term the node had already adopted and left, which is what a restart would recover. I am not asserting anything new this turn; I am asking the same experiment to answer twice.
